name: Hitachi, Ltd.
note: Kit sponsor (front, chest) of Kashiwa Reysol 2026-27 per https://www.reysol.co.jp/news/goods/202627-4.html . Left unrated for a maintainer: the owner is sourced (hitachi-ltd-shareholders: listed in Tokyo and Nagoya; the largest holders are trust-bank accounts, GOVERNMENT OF NORWAY holds 1.69%, and government and municipality holders 0.00%), but the company test isn't settled. On 6 September 2019 Japan's Immigration Services Agency issued Hitachi, Ltd. an improvement order under the Technical Intern Training Act for making foreign technical interns at its Kasado works (Kudamatsu, Yamaguchi) do work outside their training plan; after the July 2018 inspection no new training plans were approved there, and many interns who could not renew their residence status were dismissed (Nikkei, 2019-09-06, https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO49509660W9A900C1CR8000/). Hitachi and 10 group companies (12 sites) had already received improvement recommendations or guidance from the Organization for Technical Intern Training for breaches of the same act between April and September 2018 (Nikkei, 2019-03-05, https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO42034490V00C19A3CC0000/; the article names Hitachi's Omika works and Hitachi Metals, not the other companies). The Takaoka Labour Standards Inspection Office recognised in January 2018 that a Hitachi employee seconded to Hitachi Plant Services developed a mental illness because of a supervisor's conduct and more than 100 hours of overtime a month in 2015-16 (Nikkei, 2018-11-06, https://www.nikkei.com/article/DGXMZO37435230W8A101C1CR8000/). A maintainer decides whether a regulator's order over the treatment of technical interns, or a labour office's recognition of a work-related illness, is a human-rights finding under METHOD.md. The agency's own release of 2019-09-06 could not be opened (its address no longer answers), so the order rests on the Nikkei report. No record claim is written yet.
